groups.title: Launch recovery — the 497 Not Live parts
groups.blurb: 247 Waterford + 250 Essence combos launched 30 Sep and sat Not Live for five days with "Missing Images".

tasks.title: Get the 497 launched-but-not-live parts their images
tasks.summary: Both media imports failed on 1 Oct with 1,523 and 1,366 errors. Root cause found 5 Oct: the manufacturerPartId column was blank on every row. Re-imported with it populated and both went through.
tasks.result: Waterford Complete 2,716/2,716 with 0 errors. Essence Partially Complete 2,700/2,750 — the 50 rejects were shared images already present. All 497 now Live and rendering on site.
evidence: Partner Home "Not Live" and "Launched But Not Live" cards both went from 497 to zero.
PDP W123832291 loads: $75.99 was $114.99, 67 images, Add to Cart.
PDP W123833029 loads: $73.99 was $89.99, 77 images, Add to Cart.
Control test on a long-live product confirmed the earlier 404s were real, not a broken check.

updates.text: Two Product Media imports failed. 1,523 errors (Waterford), 1,366 (Essence). Import Center offered no error download.
Raised ENRICH-1492404 and ENRICH-1492407 asking Wayfair to load the images for us.
Ruled out the image URLs: all 1,061 unique Dropbox links return HTTP 200 image/jpeg, 2500x2500, 0.5-4 MB, no throttling across 40 rapid fetches.
One-SKU test isolated the cause. A file with manufacturerPartId blank returns "No Valid Changes", 0 submitted. The identical file with the ID populated imported 11/11 clean.
Re-imported both batches. 5,416 of 5,466 rows accepted.
PDPs 404'd for about two hours after going Live, then came good — storefront propagation lag, not a fault.

tasks.title: ENRICH-1492821 — PMP tool: error download and template guidance
tasks.summary: The ticket that actually matters. Two asks, both about stopping this recurring.
asks: Enable the Import Center error download. The page says to "use the download error function from the Actions column" but that column only contains a delete icon — re-checked on a Partially Complete import, still absent. Had it worked on 1 Oct we would have found the cause in minutes rather than five days and three tickets.
Correct the template guidance. manufacturerPartId is labelled Conditional, required for UPDATE and DELETE. It is clearly required for UPLOAD too, and a blank value fails the row silently.

updates.text: Raised with both failed files and a live Import Center screenshot attached.
Updated to say we found the cause ourselves and narrowed the ask to the two items above.

next: If the size-chip problem below is confirmed as a Wayfair-side bug, add it to this ticket.

learned.title: manufacturerPartId is required for UPLOAD, not just UPDATE and DELETE
learned.text: A blank value fails every row with no usable message — status reads "No Valid Changes" or "Failed". Get the IDs from Product Management → Export All → Update Product Identifiers and paste them into column E before any media import.

learned.title: The Dropbox image URLs are fine and reusable
learned.text: Links of the form dl.dropboxusercontent.com/scl/fo/.../FILE.jpg?rlkey=...&dl=0 work. The dl=0 suffix is not a problem on that host, uppercase .JPG is fine, and reusing one URL across many parts is fine — a single size-chart image served all 250 Essence combos.

learned.title: Never delete rows from a PMP export
learned.text: The isMediaChanged column is a formula referencing its own row. Deleting rows breaks those references and the whole import is rejected. Keep every row and set Action only on the ones you want to change.

learned.title: "Lead Eligible" is a capability flag, not the lead assignment
learned.text: It reads Yes on almost every image including swatches. Multiple lead-eligible images is normal and is not a defect.

learned.title: Catalogue status and the storefront are not the same thing
learned.text: Products showed Live in Partner Home about two hours before their PDPs stopped returning 404. Check the customer page, not just the dashboard — and run a control on a known-good product so a site-wide problem is not mistaken for a broken check.
